brokers.name: California DROP: one request to every registered broker
brokers.notes: For California residents. You verify and submit one deletion request on the state's own site, and it goes to every data broker registered in California. You do this yourself; UnsubVault never sees it. Check the site for how and when brokers process it.

brokers.name: Spokeo
brokers.notes: Find your own listing on the site first, then paste its page address into the opt-out form. Expect a confirmation email. These sites often re-add people, so re-check in a few months.

brokers.name: Acxiom
brokers.notes: A large marketing-data broker that sells lists used for mail and email targeting.

brokers.name: LexisNexis consumer portal
brokers.notes: Risk and identity data used by employers, insurers and others. Use the portal to see and limit what is shared.

brokers.name: LiveRamp
brokers.notes: Advertising data matching. Use the opt-out section on its privacy page.

brokers.name: Experian marketing opt-out
brokers.notes: Limits Experian's use of your data for marketing lists. Separate from your credit file.

brokers.name: OptOutPrescreen (credit card and insurance offers)
brokers.notes: The official way to stop prescreened credit and insurance offers in the mail. You can opt out for five years or permanently.

brokers.name: DMAchoice (junk mail)
brokers.notes: Reduces catalog and advertising mail from participating marketers.

brokers.name: National Do Not Call Registry
brokers.notes: Stops most telemarketing calls to your number. Scammers ignore it, but legitimate marketers must honor it.

brokers.name: Have I Been Pwned: check where your email leaked
brokers.notes: Not a removal. Shows which known data breaches include your email address, which is the most likely source of the spam in your Junk folder. Consider signing up for its breach alerts.
